subject: Re: Order form — Term, auto-renew, and termination handbook
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form follow-up: term & auto-renew questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. A couple of items Procurement needs clarity on before we proceed:

- Notice window for non-renewal: Acme typically requires a 60-day notice prior to auto-renew, but the current draft references 90 days. Can we confirm Redwood's flexibility here?
- Termination for Convenience (TfC): we'd like an explicit transition assistance commitment (data export + limited runbook assistance) and a defined post-termination access window so our teams can complete offboarding.
- Early termination economics: Acme requests that any TfC payment be limited to the pro-rated unused pre-paid portion rather than a fixed termination fee.

We're aiming to sign before the end of the month; these three items are blockers for Procurement. I've attached our suggested redlines to the order form for your legal team to review.

Attachments: ACME_Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call this week? I propose Wed afternoon.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Senior Procurement Manager, AcmeCloud
sarah.lin@acmecloud.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form follow-up: term & auto-renew questions

Ben/Karthik — forwarding Acme's procurement note and redlines. Quick summary of asks:

1) Notice window: Acme wants 60 days vs our current 90-day standard in the order form.
2) TfC: transition assistance commitment and a defined access window post-termination.
3) Early termination calculation: pro-rated unused portion only.

Proposed negotiation stance:
- Move to 60 days for this customer (pilot -> likely to scale); our typical ops can handle a 60-day offboarding with runbook support.
- For TfC, offer transition assistance limited to 30 days of continued access + one week of runbook handover calls from Solutions (no code migration services).
- For the fee, accept pro-rated refund of unused prepaid portion for non-annual committed pilots; for annual prepay enterprise deals we typically apply a short-service continuation or 30-day payout.

I've drafted a short "Termination Runbook" with the tasks Solutions will need to complete (attached). If Legal (Marissa) is comfortable with the language, we can accept the 60-day notice and formalize the runbook in the order form as an appendix.

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you review the attached runbook and the customer's redlines?
- Ben/Karthik: confirm commercial acceptance of pro-rated refund for this deal (ACME-3452).
- Evelyn: I'll schedule Wed 3pm PT with Acme unless you want a different time.

Attachments: Termination_Runbook_v1.docx (docx), Redwood_OrderForm_v3_marked.pdf (pdf)

—
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form follow-up: term & auto-renew questions

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick reply and the runbook. We reviewed the proposed concessions internally. Two follow-ups from our side:

- Acme will accept a 60-day notice for non-renewal provided Redwood commits to the transition assistance as a binding order form appendix. Specifically: one week of knowledge-transfer calls + access to our data export APIs for 30 days post-termination.
- Regarding the refund: Procurement will accept a pro-rated refund for unused prepaid amounts for pilots and mid-sized contracts. For larger annual commitments we reserve the right to request a short service continuation payment (30 days) if applicable.

I've attached a lightly edited set of redlines that reflects the above language. We'd like the legal language to be explicit (section references preferred).

Can you confirm Redwood will add the runbook as Appendix B and include the 30-day post-termination access window? If yes, we'll get Legal to clear it on our side and sign.

Attachments: ACME_Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Sarah

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form follow-up: term & auto-renew questions

Thanks everyone — quick decision and ops asks.

Legal/commercial decision: Redwood will agree to the customer's requested model for this order form (ACME-3452) with these firm concessions:

- Notice window: 60 days (replace 90).
- Termination for Convenience: include explicit Appendix B (Termination Runbook) with committed one-week KT calls and guidance; provide 30 days post-termination API/data access for exports.
- Early termination economics: pro-rated refund of unused prepaid portion for this deal; if customer upgrades to a committed annual enterprise license later we will revisit commercial remedy (standard 30-day service continuation payout) at that time.

Marissa — please draft a short addendum (Appendix B) that references the runbook and the 30-day post-termination access window. Keep the language narrowly scoped to transition assistance (no migration/coding services). Sarah, once Marissa posts the addendum I'll send an updated marked order form and a DocuSign envelope.

Operational asks: Karthik/solutions team please prepare the runbook tasks: list of exports we support, expected data formats, and a small checklist for cache/kv cleanup. We need to be ready to deliver in case they terminate within the first 12 months.

I'll be on the call Wed 3pm PT — Evelyn, please confirm and send calendar invite to Acme.

—
Ben Carter
VP, Account Management, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
